item.content:encoded:
I'm a bit conflicted here. On one hand, this is fairly well-written and the pacing is fine in most places (although some parts could use a but of trimming), the creature itself is also pretty cool in its origin. It has certain atmosphere to it.

On the other? As others have pointed out, the ending is pretty dull compared to the buildup, instead of providing some scary implication or new information for us to theorise, it simply retells the thing's effects, as it was already mentioned that folks could see him IRL and that last occurrence wasn't vastly different from anything that came before it.

The dream section also felt kinda lacking. It's really nothing new to have nightmares about a scary monster eating children, with the location also being very typical for this type of dreams. It might've been a good opportunity for the cyclops to shine, but he just behaves like a regular murder monster.

I'll stick with novote on this one.

UPD: The new ending is better than the previous one, admittedly. I'll think about this more, but I do think it's heading in the right direction.

item.title: Re: +1
item.content:encoded: …That's a really cool take. I think that's my headcanon as well.

I wish Eye-Man did something more interesting than haunting people's dreams, but the overall effect of this piece is brilliant and I love the subtle but unnerving breakdown of reality.

… My headcanon is that Wondertainment is behind thus but he wasn't trying anything malicious or anything like that, it was just a really poorly implemented attempt at magical advertising.

Good concept and buildup, but the end just didn't do anything for me. I feel like you have a great idea here, it just needs something more.

Edit: The ending is better now, but still feels like something's missing. Not sure what, though.

item.content:encoded:
This one doesn't really scratch the Parawatch itch for me. A lot of things, I'm not so sure about: for one, I wasn't exactly too scared by this. It doesn't offer anything particularly exciting or new to the Parawatch scene, and multiple parts felt like it was covering the same ground that other pieces such as Sunday Dinner or Abwesenheit do (although not the most apt comparison, it still reminded me thematically of things like that). Additionally, I'm not too keen on the stinger at the end. Doesn't have much buildup and it didn't have that fridge horror moment a lot of the aforementioned Parawatch tales have. I also have complaints on how it shifts into a first-person story midway through, though that might just be a stylistic choice and I don't find it fair to point it out.

EDIT: At the author's request, I took a second look and liked the ending a lot more. As such, I have changed my vote accordingly.
